extracted.intended_audience: writers, translators, and artists submitting work to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short fiction, non-fiction, and art to Clarkesworld Magazine, including format, content preferences, rights, and submission/process rules. Covers what the editors consider acceptable, likely hard sells, and technical/art requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Word Limit: 1000-22000 words, no exceptions

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay Rate: 10¢ per word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment via PayPal or check. (International authors may request wire transfers.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres: Science fiction and fantasy. No horror, but dark SF/F is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Language: English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We accept stories from all over the world. Translations are welcome and encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights: We claim first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights (author must be willing to sign copies), and non-exclusive anthology rights for our annual Clarkesworld anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are unfamiliar with the term 'First Rights,' an explanation can be found on their linked page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story must be well-written
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be: Well-written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language is important. There is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Convenience for on-screen reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable for audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be equally effective, but not necessarily the same, in text and audio formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science fiction and fantasy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated. Fantasy can be folkloric, contemporary, surreal, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely hard sells (themes/editorial dislikes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Though no particular setting, theme, or plot is anathema to us, the following are likely hard sells:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: zombies or zombie-wannabes; sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, wicked witches, or demonic children; stories about rapists, murderers, child abusers, or cannibals; stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines; stories with a milquetoast civilian government as sole obstacle to catching depraved criminals or to uncomplicated military victory; partisan political takeover stories (Republicans, Democrats, Libertarians, Spartacist League, etc.) where they take over the world and either save or ruin it; stories in which the words 'thou' or 'thine' appear; talking cats or swords; stories where FTL travel or time travel is as easy as it is on television shows or movies; stories that depend on vestigial belief in Judeo-Christian mythology to be frightening; stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING; stories about the stuff from Scientific American three months ago; stories about your RPG character's adventures; 'funny' stories that depend on puns; stories where the protagonist is widely despised or admired simply because they are just so smart/strange; stories in an artsy-fartsy bohemia by an author who has clearly never experienced one; stories originally intended for someone's upcoming theme anthology or issue; trunk stories; stories that try to include all of the above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT email or mail submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarkesworld uses an online submissions system. The submissions form asks for your name, email address, cover letter, story title, word count, genre and story. Go to their online submissions page to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter should contain your publishing history (if any) and any other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't include a summary in your cover letter. (Joke: e.g., if you send us a first contact and happen to BE an alien, mention that.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript format and file types
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should be in standard manuscript format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be submitted in either .RTF, .DOC, or .DOCX format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, a tracking number is displayed and an automated email confirmation is sent. Use the tracking number to monitor submission status via the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query and post-submission etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on queries, revisions, and resubmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't send queries about pending submissions until after two weeks have passed; use your tracking number to check status. Don't send revisions to a submission unless they have been requested. Don't submit another story for seven days after receiving a rejection. Don't re-submit stories that have been rejected. Do not query for permission. Don't argue with rejection letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of author information
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's personal information (name, address, email, phone, or secret identity) will not be shared with anyone outside our editorial staff, except in the following situations:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if compelled by law; if threats are made against staff; if narrators require your assistance with pronunciation (email only); if established year's best editors would like to include your story in their anthology (email only); if the author has instructed us to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction submission type (query-first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not send completed articles. Instead send a query letter with the subject header NONFICTION QUERY: [title or concept] to nonfiction@clarkesworldmagazine.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no response times. They will generally only respond to queries they wish to follow-up on. A follow-up email is not a guarantee of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction pay and word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 10¢ a word up to our word limit of 2500 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction types not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some common types of non-fiction article that we are specifically not interested in receiving queries for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are: Reviews; Literary Criticism (especially if really just a review); Interviews (handled separately and generally commissioned); Reprints (every article must be original to Clarkesworld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction topics unlikely to succeed
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics or approaches unlikely to make it out of the slush pile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: explanations as to why your favorite genre/sub-genre is the best ever; attempts to categorize genre literature; convention reports; articles about why awards 'got it wrong'; online-rant organizing pieces; '10 rules for success/failure' lists; lists of the '10 best/worst/hottest/daftest/weirdest/whatever' examples; personal experiences of alien abduction presented as article; sweeping generalizations on the basis of a few personal observations; manifestos for new literary movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction style preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred style for non-fiction submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep yourself out of the article; not an academic journal (footnotes are fine but pitch for a general audience); no interviews in disguise (we want your words, not someone else's); don't bait the audience; make sure you know your topic and avoid obvious factual errors; they may fact-check when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction positives (what they like)
rubrics_metrics.description: What the editors like to see in non-fiction articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles that are thoughtful, in-depth, and well-written; subjects they haven't covered before; accompanying illustrations (check copyright); a clear passion for the subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art selection and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Each month, Clarkesworld features a single piece of artwork that will serve as the cover for online, ebook, and print editions. Our rights are restricted to the covers and marketing materials for that specific issue. All other rights remain with the artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is $300 and two copies of the print edition. Artist's bio and link to their gallery will be posted on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art style preferences and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre art doesn't have to look genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color artwork is preferred (B&W is a hard sell). Author names and header will appear on finished covers — if crucial elements appear there it will not work. Landscape artwork is preferred (works as wrap-around cover). Prefer 2D art (digital or traditional painting). Photography and photo-realistic styles are not typically used for covers. Will not consider artwork previously used for magazine or book cover (rare invited exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Artwork must be available in a 300dpi .tif.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landscape covers measure 11" wide by 8.5" high (portrait 5.5" wide by 8.5" high). Artwork for covers must include a 1/4" bleed. Do not crop your own artwork if it goes outside these margins. Artwork must not suffer when resized; pieces must work at several sizes (e.g., look muddy at 300 pixels high is bad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: How artists should submit work for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the URL of your online gallery or portfolio to Neil Clarke (art@clarkesworldmagazine.com). The editor will contact you if interested in licensing a particular piece. Portfolios will be periodically reviewed; no need to send updates unless you change the portfolio location.
